B: Hiya! Can you hear me?
A: Yes, I can hear you. Can you hear me alright? Sorry, I never know where to look on these.
B: Yeah, you're fine! I'm Ellie.
A: Leanne. Nice to meet you.
B: You too. Where are you, then?
A: Walsall. In the West Midlands.
B: Oh, no way, I've just been talking to someone from Walsall! Kelly? She works in a care home.
A: Oh, really? I don't think I know her, but it's not that small a place. Erm, where are you?
B: Barnstaple, North Devon. I'm a lifeguard at the leisure centre, and I teach the kids' swimming lessons.
A: Oh, that's lovely. I did wonder, with the hoodie. I'm a nurse, a practice nurse, at a GP surgery. So asthma clinics, diabetes reviews, baby jabs, that sort of thing.
B: Oh, that's cool. So we kind of both do first aid, yeah? Except you actually know what you're doing.
A: Well, I don't know about that. You're the one who'd be pulling someone out of the water. I'd be stood on the side, you know, panicking quietly.
B: Honestly, you don't really think when it happens. I had to do a proper rescue last summer, a lad in the deep end, and it was so quick. One second he was fine and the next he wasn't. I still think about it, like, how quick it was. Sorry, that's a bit heavy.
A: No, no, it's not. I think that's quite normal, you know, to go back over it afterwards. I do that after a difficult day. I lie there going over what I said to someone. Is he alright now, the lad?
B: Yeah, he's fine. His mum came in with a card and everything.
A: Oh, that's nice. That must have meant a lot.
B: It did, yeah. So do you do the baby injections? I'd be useless, I'd cry more than the babies.
A: I do, yes. Erm, they tend to send me the crying ones, and the nervous adults as well. I'm slow, I suppose. I don't like rushing people, which isn't ideal when you've got ten minutes.
B: That's probably why they send them to you, though! That's like me with the scared six-year-olds. You can't rush them in the water or they just won't go in, ever.
A: Yes, I think it's probably the same thing really, isn't it. Getting someone to trust you a bit.
B: Yeah, exactly. What do you do when you're not working?
A: Oh, nothing very exciting. I walk along the canal most evenings, I read a lot, crime novels mostly. I've got a little raised bed in the garden. My tomatoes haven't ripened at all this year, they're just sat there green.
B: My nan says put them in a drawer with a banana!
A: Does that work? I'll try that. Thank you.
B: I think so? Don't quote me. I surf a bit, at Croyde, and I do little watercolours of the beach. Not very good ones.
A: I bet they're better than you think. I go to Tenby most years, and sometimes North Norfolk. I like the coast, but quiet coast, you know.
B: Oh, Tenby's so pretty! All the coloured houses.
A: Yes, I've got a print of the harbour on my wall, actually. Sorry, I've gone on about myself. Is that alright?
